Package com.example.inelasticsearch.coordinator

Class CoordinatorServiceImpl

java.lang.Object
com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.DataNodeServiceImplBase
com.example.inelasticsearch.coordinator.CoordinatorServiceImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.AsyncService, io.grpc.BindableService, AutoCloseable
public class CoordinatorServiceImpl extends com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.DataNodeServiceImplBase implements AutoCloseable
Speaks the exact same DataNodeService gRPC contract as a real data node (DataNodeServiceImpl) but never touches Lucene — it's a pure router. A client (Client, or anything else that only knows the coordinator's address) can't tell it apart from talking to a single giant node; every shard-aware decision (which node(s) to call, how to merge results) happens here instead.

Holds one DataNodeClient per node in the topology for the coordinator's whole lifetime, plus a ShardCopySelector for read routing. Writes and reads use different strategies:

  • indexDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexResponse>)/bulkIndexDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexResponse>)/deleteDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteResponse>) — always route to a shard's single primary (ClusterTopology.nodeFor(int)). No replica involvement, no retry if the primary is down; that's the "primary-only writes" design.
  • search(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchResponse>) — round-robins across a shard's primary and replicas (via ShardCopySelector) so read load spreads across every live copy, and transparently falls back to the shard's other copies if whichever one was picked doesn't answer. See the method doc for the two-phase fan-out/fallback shape.

    • search

      public void search(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchRequest request, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchResponse> responseObserver)
      Two-phase scatter-gather search, load-balanced and fault-tolerant per shard:
      1. Phase 1 — round-robin fan-out. For every shard, ask ShardCopySelector.nextCandidates(int) which copy to try (cycling through primary and replicas across successive calls) and remember the full ordered candidate list for fallback. Shards are then grouped by whichever node they landed on, so a node holding several chosen shards this round still gets one scoped RPC, not one per shard — and all of those RPCs run in parallel on executor, bounded by SEARCH_FANOUT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
      2. Phase 2 — per-shard fallback. Any shard whose chosen node didn't answer gets retried, one shard at a time, against the rest of its candidate list (in ring order, skipping the copy that just failed) until one succeeds or the list is exhausted. A shard only contributes an error to the final response if every one of its copies — not just the one phase 1 happened to pick — turned out to be unreachable.

      Because each shard is only ever queried once per round (one candidate in phase 1, or one more in phase 2 on failure), merged hits are never duplicated across a shard's copies. The response is marked successful if anything came back at all; per-shard/per-node failures are concatenated into error_message rather than failing the whole request.
